from.place: the closure argument for cones and countable direct sums in the proof of the K-flat closure lemmas 07A3 and 06YR

title: Cones and countable direct sums of K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. If $(K_n^\bullet)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ is a countable family of K-flat complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], then $\bigoplus_n K_n^\bullet$ is K-flat, and the mapping cone of every morphism of K-flat complexes is K-flat.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (closure of K-flat complexes under cones and direct sums)

proof.text: For any acyclic complex A, tensoring commutes with the countable coproduct: Tot(A tensor (direct sum of K_n)) is the direct sum of Tot(A tensor K_n). The category of sheaves of O-modules is Grothendieck abelian (after replacing an essentially small site by an equivalent small one), so countable coproducts are exact: write the coproduct as the filtered colimit of its finite partial coproducts and use exactness of filtered colimits. Each summand is acyclic by K-flatness, hence the coproduct is acyclic. Since this holds for every acyclic A, the countable direct sum is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Lemma 06YR, closure under filtered colimits, applied to finite partial coproducts

proof.text: For a morphism f from K1 to K2 and its mapping cone K3, the tensor construction is additive and carries the cone triangle to the cone triangle of the tensor of f. If K1 and K2 are K-flat, then the first two tensor complexes are acyclic for every acyclic A; the tensor-triangle two-out-of-three statement [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-cone-two-out-of-three] makes the third tensor complex acyclic. Therefore the mapping cone is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex].
